issue_context.title: SecurityStampValidator reissues the session cookie and extends its expiry
issue_context.body:
Hello, I would like to bring this issue for a revisit:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/13117

We are having a similar problem in ASP.NET Core 3.1

Our session cookie is set to have:
```
 SlidingExpiration = False
 ExpireTimeSpan = 24h
```
 
For which we expect no Sliding Expiration behavior.

But even with this setting the cookie is still being recreated on a time interval matching the security stamp validation interval.

After investigation of the aspnetcore code it looks to me that by default the SecurityStampValidator reissues a new cookie when validation result is true. This on its hand extends the user login time. I would rather expect that when the security stamp validation is true, nothing should be done at least to the cookie.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Identity/Core/src/SecurityStampValidator.cs#L104-L131
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/e23fd047b4baf3480ce93d7643a897732f960557/src/Identity/Core/src/SecurityStampValidator.cs#L68-L92

review_comments: Should there be a null check on context.Options here? There's one in ValidateAsync below but I can't actually tell what that one is for.

CookieValidatePrincipalContext's base constructor ensures Options is never null. Not sure why ValidateAsync checked it, it never even references Options otherwise. I'll remove it.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/e6a5af6633f08890afbd99a6ca7687c623454768/src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/Events/BaseContext.cs#L30-L33
Ah, looks like leftovers from some refactoring during 2.0.
